method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Drug-naive children: under 12 years, 1 mg is potentially toxic; 12 years or older, more than 5 mg.** These need urgent assessment.
claims.source_text: Urgent assessment is required for all children who may have ingested the following: … In drug naive children: less than 12 years of age, an ingestion of 1 mg should be considered potentially toxic 12 years or older, an ingestion of more than 5 mg should be considered potentially toxic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children on regular risperidone: more than 5 times their current single dose (not daily dose) is potentially toxic.**
claims.source_text: In children who take risperidone on a regular basis, a dose more than 5 times their current single dose (not daily dose) should be considered potentially toxic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also assess:** any symptomatic patient · any ingestion of unknown quantity · every deliberate self-poisoning or significant accidental ingestion.
claims.source_text: Any symptomatic patient Acute ingestion of unknown quantity All children with deliberate self-poisoning or significant accidental ingestion
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Symptoms usually start within 1–2 hours and peak by 4–6 hours**, but resolution can take several days (half-life 3–30 hours). **Alcohol and cannabis may deepen CNS depression.**
claims.source_text: Symptoms generally develop within 1–2 hours and peak by 4–6 hours post ingestion … Resolution of symptoms may take several days (half-life can vary depending on an individual’s metabolism, from 3–30 hours) … Co-ingestants eg alcohol and cannabis may enhance CNS depressant effect
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild to moderate:** tachycardia and hypotension are common, with depressed mental status, somnolence and extrapyramidal symptoms.
claims.source_text: Mild to moderate toxicity: Cardiac: Tachycardia and hypotension are common CNS: Depressed mental status, somnolence and extrapyramidal symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Severe:** QTc prolongation and ventricular arrhythmia; extrapyramidal symptoms likely; respiratory depression, seizures, coma or neuroleptic malignant syndrome can occur.
claims.source_text: Severe toxicity: Cardiac: QTc prolongation, ventricular arrhythmia CNS: extrapyramidal symptoms likely Respiratory depression, seizure, or coma could potentially occur, as well as neuroleptic malignant syndrome
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen with a 12-lead ECG, BSL and paracetamol level. ECG at presentation and at 4 hours** — tachycardia can be delayed up to 20 hours.
claims.source_text: Screening: 12 lead ECG, BSL, paracetamol level … ECG at presentation and 4 hours (onset of tachycardia can be delayed up to 20 hours)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hypotension: IV fluids; if it persists, a vasopressor — norepinephrine preferred.** Avoid epinephrine and dopamine: beta stimulation may worsen hypotension with risperidone's alpha blockade.
claims.source_text: Treat hypotension with intravenous fluids. If hypotension persists administer vasopressor - norepinephrine is preferred. The manufacturer recommends avoidance of epinephrine and dopamine since beta stimulation may worsen hypotension in the setting of risperidone-induced alpha blockade
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Activated charcoal has a very limited role**; discuss with a toxicologist.
claims.source_text: Activated charcoal has a very limited role in treatment. Discuss with a toxicologist via the Poisons Information Centre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Seizures: IV benzodiazepines; add propofol or barbiturates if they recur or persist. Avoid phenytoin and fosphenytoin.**
claims.source_text: Seizure: administer IV benzodiazepines; add propofol or barbiturates if seizures recur or persist (avoid phenytoin or fosphenytoin).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Extrapyramidal symptoms — benzatropine IM or IV:** 3–12 years 0.02 mg/kg (max 1 mg); 12–18 years 1–2 mg. May be repeated in 15 minutes. EPS can appear up to several days after exposure.
claims.source_text: Extrapyramidal symptoms: may occur up to several days post exposure … Treatment: Benzatropine Dose: 3–12 years, give 0.02 mg/kg IM or IV (maximum 1 mg) 12–18 years, give 1–2 mg IM or IV May need to repeat dosing in 15 minutes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Don't discharge a child who still needs benzatropine.**
claims.source_text: Avoid discharging patients requiring ongoing doses of benzatropine
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider admission for:** every intentional overdose · symptomatic patients · overdose with cardiovascular or neurological disease.
claims.source_text: Admission should be considered for all children and adolescents with an intentional overdose symptomatic patients those with an overdose in the presence of cardiovascular or neurological disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Transfer for significant CNS depression, seizures, or any cardiovascular instability.**
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when There is significant CNS depression/seizures or any cardiovascular instability
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when GCS and ECG are normal after a period of observation. Warn that extrapyramidal movements can appear up to 3 days later.**
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when Normal GCS Normal ECG Period of observation Warn that extrapyramidal movements may occur up to 3 days later
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Before discharging an adolescent after a deliberate ingestion**, assess self-harm risk and other drug and alcohol use.
claims.source_text: Prior to discharge, adolescents who present with deliberate ingestions need a risk assessment regarding the likelihood of further ingestions or other attempts to self-harm … Assessment of other drug and alcohol use should also be undertaken
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Risperidone Poisoning' (Last Updated September 2020), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Risperidone_Poisoning/, retrieved 2026-09-23
